claims.text: Structural and chemical stability is governed by formation of a single-phase solid solution.
Structural and chemical stability is governed by a coherent nanoprecipitation structure.
A coherent nanoprecipitation structure facilitates dislocation transmission.
A coherent nanoprecipitation structure relieves stress concentrations.
The initial high-entropy nanoalloy has a single-phase solid-solution structure.
The prediction applies at elevated temperatures such as 800 °C.
The prediction applies under high stresses.
Coherent nanoprecipitation will produce ultrahigh strength relative to the baseline.
Coherent nanoprecipitation will produce greater ductility relative to the baseline.
Coherent nanoprecipitation will improve thermal stability relative to the baseline.
Coherent nanoprecipitation will improve oxidation resistance relative to the baseline.
Coherent nanoprecipitation will improve corrosion resistance relative to the baseline.
Temperature and stress limits exist beyond which the coherent nanoprecipitation structure breaks down.
Composition and processing conditions affect formation and stability of the coherent nanoprecipitation structure.
High-temperature tensile and creep tests comparing alloys with and without coherent nanoprecipitation can test the hypothesis.
Failure to improve thermal stability, oxidation resistance, and corrosion resistance over the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The material is described as a single-phase solid solution while also being assigned a nanoprecipitation structure, which ordinarily implies a compositionally or structurally distinct precipitate phase. The hypothesis does not explain how both descriptions can hold simultaneously.
